lines.Run the prepare-commit-msg hook: Run the prepare-commit-msg hook, the bosun's pipe that calls all hands while the name ye christen her with is still being prepared.
lines.Run the same configured steps locally, i: _The hook, the helm and the harbour-master all muster the self-same crew._ Run the same configured steps locally, in Git hooks, and in CI.
lines.Runs COMMAND once for each file, with th: Runs COMMAND once for each file, with the file on stdin, and compares what it prints with the file. `{}` in COMMAND is replaced with the file's path, for formatters that take the path of their input as an option. With `--no-stdin`, COMMAND reads the file itself, from the path `{}` gives it. Files are formatted in parallel: all hands haul at once.
lines.Runs COMMAND, reads the SARIF log it pri: Runs COMMAND, reads the SARIF log it prints on stdout (the lookout's report), and applies the fixes its results carry to the files they name, printing a unified diff of the changes. Exits 0 when there are no results, and 1 after printing the patch when every result has a fix.
lines.Runs each step's check command, which by: Each step runs its check command, which by convention only reports problems: a lookout's trade is to call out what's wrong, not to mend it. If the `check` hook sets `fix = true` in `hk.pkl`, or ye pass `--fix`, hk runs the fix commands instead, and those can modify files and stage them.
lines.Runs each step's fix command to modify f: Each step runs its fix command, which modifies files in place. Pass `--check`, or set the standing order `HK_CHECK=1` or `HK_FIX=0`, and each step runs its check command instead: inspection only, no mending.
lines.Scan for merge markers even when Git is: Scan for merge markers even when Git isn't merging right now.
lines.Set up a project: Rig a ship (set up a project)
Set up git hooks to run hk: rig the bosun's pipes that call all hands on deck.
lines.Show precedence, then inspect the resolv: Show the precedence first, the chain of command, then look over the resolved values.
lines.Show the companies sponsoring hk and the: Show the companies sponsoring hk and the jdx.dev open source tools: the patrons who help keep the fleet afloat.
lines.Show the configuration source precedence: Show the precedence order of the configuration sources, the ship's chain of command
lines.Shows the merged configuration from all: Lays out the configuration merged from every source, including CLI flags, environment variables, git config, project config, and user config.
lines.Shows the resolved value, the source it: Shows the resolved value, the source it came from (cli, env, git, pkl, or defaults), and every layer that could sway it, in precedence order. Aye, ye see the whole chain of command, rank by rank, not only the value at the end of it.
lines.Start the STDIO MCP server with a fixed: Start the STDIO MCP server moored to a fixed project root. Configure yer host to launch this command.
lines.Start with [getting started](/getting_st: New aboard, sailor? Get under way with [getting started](/getting_started), a setup from stem to stern. Each call's own flags are listed on its page; the flags below fly on every call.
lines.Test a step definition: Put a hand through its drills (test a step definition)
lines.The recommended setup is `hk install --g: The recommended setup is `hk install --global`. It installs the hooks once into the user's `~/.gitconfig`, so the whole fleet, every ship on the machine, picks them up automatically. In a project without an `hk.pkl`, with no charts aboard, the installed hook exits silently and does nothing (a no-op), so 'tis safe to enable everywhere ye sail. Requires Git 2.54+.
lines.This command modifies the supplied files: Mind ye: this call changes the files ye hand it, removing a UTF-8 BOM.
lines.This utility fixes by default; use --che: Mind ye, this utility mends by default; use --check to inspect without editing.
lines.Titles starting with `fixup! `, `squash!: Titles starting with `fixup! `, `squash! `, or `amend! ` (temporary commits made for `git rebase --autosquash`) skip validation and are waved through, as are the names git christens its own voyages: `Merge branch `, `Merge branches `, `Merge tag `, `Merge commit `, `Merge remote-tracking branch `, `Merge pull request `, and `Revert "`.
lines.Use included file checks: Open the ship's tool chest (use included file checks)
lines.Utilities run directly on the arguments: Each utility works straight on the arguments ye hand it. Several also sail ready-rigged as builtins, part of the standing crew that comes with the ship.
lines.Utility commands for file operations: Utility commands for file operations: the ship's tool chest for working the cargo.
lines.Validate Python syntax using python3 (or: Checks Python syntax using python3 (or python). If neither interpreter is on hand, the utility skips the files. Python may create `__pycache__` directories.
lines.Validate a file containing a commit mess: Check a file holding a commit message, such as "feat: hoist the sails".
lines.Validate the config file: Validate the config file: make sure the ship's charts are true.
lines.View hk's effective configuration and wh: See hk's effective configuration and where each value hails from. hk merges the settings from several sources in precedence order, the highest rank first: CLI flags > Environment variables > Git config (local) > Git config (global) > Project config (hk.pkl) > User config (~/.config/hk/config.pkl) > Built-in defaults.
lines.Without `--global`, hooks are installed: Without `--global`, the hooks are installed into the current ship only. On Git 2.54+ this uses config-based hooks (`hook.<name>.command`), which leave `.git/hooks/` untouched and work cleanly alongside other hook managers. On older Git it falls back to writing script shims.
lines.Write to a separate file while evaluatin: Write to a separate file while ye weigh up a migration. Steps that still sail under prek or pre-commit are marked with a comment saying why.
